items: National Commissions for SCs / STs / Backward Classes

parts.t: Public Service Commissions: origin, appointment and removal
items: **First Public Service Commission:** first established under the **GoI Act 1919** (**1 Oct 1926**).
Removal for misbehavior requires a binding Supreme Court inquiry (Art. 317); Parliament has no role.
Governor appoints, but only the President can remove an SPSC Chairman/Member.
**SPSC Chairman removal:** an SPSC Chairman is appointed by the **Governor**, but can be removed ONLY by the **President** under **Article 317**.
**APPSC (AP Public Service Commission):** established **1 Nov 1956**; **Art. 315**; merger of the Andhra + Hyderabad PSCs.

lectures.title: Election Commission of India: status, composition and functions

items: **Constitutional status:** permanent, independent, constitutional body under **Part XV (Articles 324–329)**.
**Established:** on **25 January 1950** (celebrated annually as **National Voters' Day** since 2011).
**Article 324(1):** vests the superintendence, direction, and control of elections in the Election Commission of India (ECI).
**Mandate covers elections to:** Parliament (Lok Sabha & Rajya Sabha), State Legislatures (Assemblies & Councils), President, and Vice-President.
**Local body elections** (Panchayats and Municipalities) are NOT conducted by ECI; they fall under the **State Election Commission (SEC)** under **Articles 243K & 243ZA**.
**Composition:** 1 Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) + 2 Election Commissioners (multi-member body established continuously since **1 October 1993**).
**Equal status:** all three have equal powers, salary equivalent to Supreme Court Judges, and decide by majority.
**Tenure:** 6 years or up to 65 years of age, whichever is earlier.
**Removal of the CEC:** removed only in like manner and on the same grounds as a Supreme Court Judge (**Art. 324(5)**).
**Removal of other ECs & Regional Commissioners:** removed by the President on the recommendation of the CEC.

parts.t: Electoral rolls, suffrage and the right to vote
items: **Art. 325:** single general electoral roll; no discrimination based on religion, race, caste, or sex.
**Art. 326:** Universal Adult Suffrage for Lok Sabha and Legislative Assemblies.
**Voting age:** reduced from 21 to 18 years via the **61st Constitutional Amendment Act, 1988** (effective 1989).
**Nature of the right to vote and the right to be elected / to contest:** Legal / Statutory Rights (**Kuldip Nayar v. Union of India, 2006**), NOT Fundamental Rights.

parts.t: Disqualification, parties and the Model Code
items: **Disqualification of MPs (Art. 103):** decided by the President based on the binding opinion of the ECI.
**Disqualification of MLAs/MLCs (Art. 192):** decided by the Governor based on the binding opinion of the ECI.

**Party registration & symbols:** registers political parties under **RPA 1951**; allots symbols and decides recognition under the **Election Symbols (Reservation and Allotment) Order, 1968**; adjudicates party merger/split disputes.
**Model Code of Conduct (MCC):** formulated and enforced by ECI from the date of election schedule announcement (ECI-formulated guideline, NOT an Act of Parliament).
**MCC in force:** comes into force immediately upon the formal announcement of the election schedule by the ECI.

parts.t: What the ECI does not do
items: **Notification:** election notifications are issued by the **President** (Parliament) or **Governor** (State Legislature), NOT by the ECI. ECI only recommends dates and determines / administers the schedule.
**Presiding Officers:** chosen/elected internally by the respective Houses, NOT conducted by ECI.

**Dispute adjudication:** handled exclusively by the Judiciary via election petitions, NOT by ECI; Presidential/Vice-Presidential disputes are handled exclusively by the Supreme Court under **Art. 71**.

**Delimitation Commission vs ECI:** constituency delimitation is executed by an independent Delimitation Commission set up under parliamentary law, whose orders cannot be questioned in court or modified by legislatures.

lectures.title: Election law: RPA 1950 and 1951, parties, delimitation and reforms

parts.t: RPA 1950 and RPA 1951: the key distinction
items: **RPA, 1950:** deals with the allocation of seats, delimitation of constituencies, voter qualifications, preparation of electoral rolls, and the detailed composition of State Legislative Councils (Art. 171(2) ↔ Section 10 & 3rd Schedule of RPA 1950).
**RPA, 1951:** deals with the actual conduct of elections, qualifications/disqualifications of candidates, registration of political parties, corrupt practices, election petitions, and disputes.
Allocation of Lok Sabha, Assembly & Council seats
Registration of electors & preparation of rolls
**Section 33(7) of RPA, 1951 (contesting seat limits):** a candidate can contest from a maximum of 2 constituencies: 2 Parliamentary or 2 Assembly constituencies at a time.
**Origin & context:** following the 1991 elections where Devi Lal contested from 3 Lok Sabha seats, RPA 1951 was amended in **1996** (capping the limit at 2).
**Forfeiture of security deposit:** occurs if a candidate fails to secure more than **1/6th** of total valid votes polled.
**Rajya Sabha domicile / voter requirement:** prior to 2003, a candidate contesting for Rajya Sabha had to be an elector in that particular State.
**2003 Amendment:** removed this requirement; any registered elector in India can contest from any State. Upheld by the SC in **Kuldip Nayar (2006)**.

**Death of a contesting candidate (1996 Amendment):** elections are no longer countermanded automatically upon the death of a candidate; recognized political parties are permitted to nominate a replacement within a set timeframe.
**Dinesh Goswami Committee (1990):** set up on Electoral Reforms; recommended state funding of elections, EVMs, and the measures subsequently enacted in the 1996 RPA Amendment.

parts.t: Registration and recognition of political parties
items: **Party registration:** political parties are registered by the Election Commission of India (ECI) under **Section 29A of RPA 1951**.
**Recognition:** recognized as National/State parties under the **Election Symbols (Reservation and Allotment) Order, 1968** (NOT by Parliament, Law Ministry, or President).

**Party registration authority:** always eliminate options attributing political party registration to the Ministry of Law & Justice or Parliament. It is strictly executed by the Election Commission of India (ECI).

**Votes + seats:** at least **6%** of the total valid votes polled in **four or more States** in a Lok Sabha general election or State Legislative Assembly election, AND at least **4 Lok Sabha seats** from any State or States; OR
**Seats:** at least **2%** of the total seats in the Lok Sabha (which equals **11 seats**), and these elected members must come from at least **3 different States**; OR
**State Party status:** officially recognized as a State Party in at least **4 different States**.
**First President of Bharatiya Jana Sangh:** Dr. Shyama Prasad Mukherjee.
**First President of BJP:** Atal Bihari Vajpayee (1980).
**Congress(I):** formed by Indira Gandhi on **2 Jan 1978** (by splitting INC).
**Telugu Desam Party (TDP):** founded by **N.T. Rama Rao (NTR)** on **29 March 1982**.
**Continuous Congress rule in AP broken:** **1983** (by the newly formed party, TDP).
**Nadendla Bhaskara Rao:** formed the Democratic Telugu Desam Party.
**Constitution:** constituted by the Central Government under an Act of Parliament (headed by a retired SC Judge + CEC + State SECs).
**Finality of orders:** orders have the force of law and cannot be called in question in any court (**Art. 329**). When laid before Parliament/Assemblies, orders cannot be modified.
**Four Delimitation Commissions** constituted so far: **1952, 1963, 1973, and 2002**.
First used: Noksen Assembly by-election, Nagaland (4 Sept 2013)
Sept 2013; directed by Supreme Court on 27 September 2013 (PUCL v. Union of India)
**Election reforms chronology:** EVM -> EPIC Voter ID -> VVPAT -> NOTA.
**Simultaneous Elections (ONOE) Articles:** potentially requires amending **Arts. 83, 85, 172, 174, and 356**.
**Constitutional status:** permanent, independent, quasi-judicial constitutional body under **Article 280 (Part XII)**.
**Constituted by** the President of India every 5 years or earlier as deemed necessary (not strictly/rigidly every 5 years).
**First Commission:** constituted by the President's order of **22 November 1951**, under Chairman **K.C. Neogy**.
**Core function:** anchor of Fiscal Federalism; recommends the distribution of net tax proceeds between the Union and States, and the allocation among States.
**Composition (Art. 280(1)):** total 5 members -> 1 Chairman + 4 other members appointed by the President.
**Qualifications (Art. 280(2)):** determined by Parliament by law (**Finance Commission Act, 1951**), NOT determined by the President or Union Cabinet.
**Nature:** possesses powers of a civil court regarding summoning and production of documents (quasi-judicial character).
5 Members (Chairman + 4); Parliament by law determines qualifications (NOT President); First: K.C. Neogy.
**Finance Commission qualifications:** the President appoints the Chairman and members, but their qualifications are prescribed by Parliament by law (Finance Commission Act, 1951).
**Devolution of taxes:** distribution of the net proceeds of divisible Union taxes between Centre and States, and allocation among States.
**Grants-in-aid:** principles governing grants-in-aid of State revenues out of the Consolidated Fund of India (**Art. 275**).

**Local bodies resource augmentation:** measures needed to augment the Consolidated Fund of a State to supplement the resources of Panchayats and Municipalities based on recommendations of the State Finance Commission.
**Sound finance:** any other matter referred to it by the President in the interest of sound public finance.
**Submission of report (Art. 281):** submits its report to the President, who causes it to be laid before both Houses of Parliament along with an explanatory memorandum on action taken.
**Trap:** the report is laid by the **President**, NOT the Finance Minister.

parts.t: Union Finance Commission and State Finance Commission

items: Recommended a historic increase in States' share of net divisible taxes from 32% to 42% (+10 percentage points)
**Art. 275:** statutory grants-in-aid to States (principles recommended by the Finance Commission under Art. 280).
**Art. 282:** discretionary grants made by the Union or a State for any public purpose outside its legislative purview.
**Fiscal disputes:** legal/constitutional disputes between the Centre and States are resolved by the Supreme Court under Original Jurisdiction (**Art. 131**), NOT by the Finance Commission.

lectures.title: Attorney General of India and Advocate General of the State

parts.t: Attorney General: status, appointment and tenure
items: **Constitutional status:** highest law officer of the Government of India under **Part V (Article 76)**.
**Appointment:** appointed by the President of India.
**Tenure:** holds office during the pleasure of the President (no fixed constitutional tenure).
**Removal & resignation:** can be removed at any time by the President; resignation is submitted to the President (traditionally resigns when the Council of Ministers changes).
**Remuneration:** determined by the President (not fixed by Parliament or the Constitution).
**Primary role:** advises the Government of India on legal matters and performs other legal duties referred by the President.

parts.t: Attorney General: qualifications and right of audience
items: **Qualifications (equivalent to a Supreme Court Judge):** must be a citizen of India, AND has been a High Court Judge for at least 5 years, OR an advocate of a High Court for at least 10 years, OR is a distinguished jurist in the opinion of the President.
**Right of audience:** enjoys the right of audience in all courts within the territory of India while performing official duties.

parts.t: Attorney General: rights and privileges in Parliament (Art. 88)
items: **Speak:** under Article 88, the AGI has the right to speak in either House of Parliament (Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha).
**Joint sittings:** the right to take part in the proceedings of joint sittings of Parliament.
**Committees:** the right to be named a member of and participate in any Parliamentary Committee.
**Privileges:** entitled to all privileges and immunities of a Member of Parliament under **Article 105(4)**.
**Right to vote trap:** speak in Parliament - YES; participate in Parliamentary Committees - YES; vote on any motion/bill - **NO**.

parts.t: Attorney General: executive status and the Solicitor General
items: **Executive status:** the Attorney General is not a member of the Central Cabinet and is not considered a full-time government servant (private legal practice is not completely debarred, subject to government restrictions).
**Solicitor General & Additional Solicitors General:** non-constitutional posts created to assist the Attorney General.
**Constitutional status:** highest law officer and official legal adviser to the State Government under **Part VI (Article 165)**.
**Appointment (Art. 165(1)):** appointed by the Governor of the State (trap: appointed by the Governor, NOT the President).
**Qualifications:** must be qualified to be appointed as a Judge of a High Court (**Art. 217**).
**Tenure (Art. 165(3)):** holds office during the pleasure of the Governor (no fixed constitutional tenure; NOT during the pleasure of the Cabinet or Chief Minister).
**Duties (Art. 165(2)):** advises the State Government upon legal matters and performs other legal duties assigned by the Governor or the Constitution.

parts.t: Advocate General: rights in the State Legislature (Art. 177)
items: **Floor participation:** under Article 177, the Advocate General has the right to speak in and take part in the proceedings of both Houses of the State Legislature (Legislative Assembly and Legislative Council).
**Committees:** the right to be named a member of and participate in any State Legislative Committee.
**Membership status:** is NOT a member of the State Legislature.
**Trap:** speak in State Legislature - YES; participate in proceedings - YES; vote on any motion/bill - **NO**.

parts.t: Attorney General, Advocate General and Solicitor General compared
items: Union Government (Assists the AGI / Attorney General)
No legislative floor rights; no floor rights in Parliament
**Appointing authority traps:** High Court Judges: appointed by the President; Advocate General: appointed by the Governor.
**Tenure & removal traps:** a statement claiming tenure is during the "Pleasure of the State Cabinet / Chief Minister" is FALSE; correct formulation: Pleasure of the Governor.
